bib.title: Efficient Large-Scale Language Model Training on GPU Clusters Using Megatron-LM

question: How should tensor, pipeline and data parallelism be combined to maximise training throughput of very large LMs at a given batch size while keeping strict optimizer semantics?
hypothesis: Composing pipeline parallelism across servers, tensor parallelism within a server and data parallelism scales to thousands of GPUs at high utilisation.
contributions: PTD-P: composition of pipeline, tensor and data parallelism
Analytical study of interactions between parallelism dimensions, microbatch size and activation recomputation, with three takeaways
Scatter/gather communication optimisation and fused-kernel computation optimisations
Open-source Megatron-LM implementation; 1T-parameter model at 502 petaFLOP/s on 3072 GPUs

method.summary: PTD-P extension to Megatron-LM (PyTorch, NCCL) combining inter-node pipeline parallelism (PipeDream-Flush 1F1B, optionally interleaved), intra-node tensor parallelism and data parallelism. Throughput of GPT models of 1.7B to 1T parameters measured on the Selene A100 cluster, plus ablations and a ZeRO-3 comparison.
method.task: distributed pretraining throughput (systems benchmark of GPT models)

other.1T model: 128 layers, hidden 25600, 160 heads, t=8, p=64, 3072 GPUs, batch 3072

training.tokens: not trained; time estimated for 300B (GPT-3) and 450B (1T) tokens
training.hardware: Selene: 8x NVIDIA 80GB A100 per node, NVLink/NVSwitch, 8 x 200Gbps HDR InfiniBand HCAs per node, 3-level fat tree with 850 switches; up to 3072 GPUs (384 nodes)
training.wall_clock: estimated 34 days (GPT-3 175B, 300B tokens, 1024 GPUs); 84 days (1T, 450B tokens, 3072 GPUs)

other.note: Only throughput is measured; no convergence run is reported. Optimizer, LR and data are not stated.

metrics.name: Achieved teraFLOP/s per GPU
metrics.definition: FLOPs per iteration (eq. 3, GEMMs only, includes recomputation) divided by end-to-end iteration time incl. data loading, optimizer, communication, logging

eval.protocol: Throughput of training iterations; repeats, seeds and variance are not stated.

results.claim: A 1T-parameter GPT reaches 502 petaFLOP/s aggregate on 3072 A100 GPUs, 52% of peak.
results.setup: GPT 1T params (128 layers, hidden 25600), t=8, p=64, batch 3072, seq 2048, mixed precision, interleaved schedule + scatter/gather, Selene
results.quote: an aggregate throughput of 502 petaFLOP/s, on a GPT model [11] with a trillion parame-

results.claim: Per-GPU end-to-end throughput for the 1T model is 163 teraFLOP/s.
results.setup: Same 1T-parameter configuration, includes communication, data processing and optimisation
results.quote: end-to-end training throughput of 163 teraFLOP/s per GPU

results.claim: PTD-P beats ZeRO-3 by 70% when GPU count is doubled at fixed batch size, for 175B and 530B models.
results.setup: GPT-3 175B and 530B, global batch fixed, ZeRO-3 without tensor/pipeline parallelism, DeepSpeed integration
results.quote: PTD-P outperforms ZeRO-3 by 70% for both models due to less cross-node communication

results.claim: Estimated end-to-end training time for GPT-3 175B on 1024 A100s is 34 days.
results.setup: 300B tokens, batch 1536, 140 teraFLOP/s per GPU, time ~ 8TP/(nX)
results.quote: the time required to train this model is 34 days
results.note: Estimate from throughput, not a completed run

results.claim: Estimated training time for the 1T model is 84 days.
Interleaved schedule improves throughput by as much as 10% over prior schedules at comparable memory.
results.setup: 175B GPT, 96 GPUs, small batch sizes, with scatter/gather (Fig 12); gap closes as batch grows
results.quote: improve throughput by as much as 10% compared to previously-proposed schedules

results.claim: Scatter/gather optimisation raises throughput up to 11% for communication-heavy schedules.
results.setup: GPT-3 175B, 96 A100, interleaved schedule, large batch
results.quote: We see an improvement of up to 11% in throughput

results.claim: Operator fusion lifts GPT-3 175B from 113 to 135 teraFLOP/s per GPU (19%).
results.quote: throughput increased by 19% with fusion (113 teraFLOP/s per GPU to 135 teraFLOP/s per GPU)

results.claim: Activation recomputation costs up to 33% throughput at small batch but enables batches giving up to 2x higher throughput.
results.quote: activation recomputation leads to up to 33% lower throughput

results.claim: DeepSpeed's earlier 1T result reached 36% of peak versus 52% here.
results.setup: V100 hardware; compared by the authors

results.claim: Smallest model (1.7B, 32 GPUs) achieves 137 teraFLOP/s, 44% of peak; per-GPU efficiency rises with model size.
results.setup: Table 1 first row, t=1 p=1, batch 512
results.quote: We achieve 52% of peak device throughput for the largest model, and 44% of peak device throughput for the smallest model.
results.table: Table 1, row 1.7B, column Achieved teraFLOP/s per GPU

results.claim: Optimal microbatch size is 4 in the analytic model (1B GPT) and 2 empirically for the 91B model.
results.quote: We see that the best microbatch size is 2 for this model

results.claim: Trillion-parameter checkpoint is 13.8 TB; save reaches 273 GB/s.
results.quote: the trillion-parameter model has a checkpoint of size 13.8 terabytes

limits: Throughput only: no convergence or accuracy run, and optimizer, learning rate and data are not stated.
No automatic search of parallelism strategies; heuristics only.
Needs an optimised stack: NVLink inside nodes and high-bandwidth InfiniBand across; results depend on Selene.
Synchronous flushes only; asynchronous/bounded-staleness pipelines deferred.
ZeRO-3 compared without model parallelism; authors concede combining could improve it.
Training times are estimates from throughput, not completed runs.
No variance or repeat counts reported.
